smimon wrote: Can't say I'm too displeased with this EU trade, one for the scrap book for sure, in within 0.1 pips of the bottom.

Hey pal. I currently watch 7 pairs, the most liquid - AU, EJ, EU, GU, UCAD, UJ and Gold. UCHF is out the window now after last week.

I try to sit down about 0730GMT, there are always some great setups forming off the tail end of the Asian session, ready for a burst of liquidity at the London open at 0800. It's often possible to be done for the day in terms of profit by 0900 if I catch the right winners. Sometimes there's some good GBP news at 0930 which I'll trade the aftermath of. I'm away at from the charts 1000 to the gym, lunch, because not a lot usually happens 1030 - 1300, and then I'm back at the desk to catch whatever US news is at 1330, and then the US open at 1430. Through til about 1630, and then done. I'll sometimes check what's happening about 2300 just before bed, to see if anything is setting up ahead of the Asian session, so that I can take an entry or set a PO for an overnight trade chance.

I'm sat in front of the desk a lot at the moment, because I'm still learning, but eventually the less trading the better.

Every H1 and H4 new bar, my charts automatically flip into H1/H4 so I can check the HTF PA, make sure I'm not missing anything obvious.

Thank you for the kind words, they're very much appreciated.

I remember when I first quit work to start trading, and reality set in very quickly that I didn't have a clue what I was doing, and couldn't seem to find anything on the web that was of much help. Everyone had a different method, these indicators, or this type of supply and demand, volume profiling - I chopped and changed, tried everything under the sun, and couldn't get anything remotely resembling consistent results. I began to despair at one point that I'd ever be able to make it as a trader, or if I did, it would be scraping by on a statistical edge, barely winning more than I lost. They were dark days.

My friend put my on to RTM at the very end of September, and at first I was sceptical -I'd tried so many other things, and I thought this was just going to be more of the same, something which people raved about working, but ended up useless. I stuck with it though, read as many journals as I could find, went back through my chart histories doing markup after markup. I remember a couple of months in, when I suddenly started being able to make sense of the charts to some degree, the feeling of hope that I was actually going to be able to fulfil my dream of getting out of the rate race, and make myself wealthy working on my own terms.

There are so many friendly, helpful people on here, willing to give away knowledge they've spent 1000s of hours accumulating, for no reason other than the common good, that I feel it's the least I can do to try and do the same. I'm getting nearer to the end of the bulk of the main learning process now, but I'm still making a lot of mistakes, and I've got 6 months left or so before the wolves are at the door, so I'd rather just take an extra few weeks to really try and get to grips with things before sticking my cash on the line. I want it to be as stress-free as possible

smimon wrote: This is an example of what I mean - this PO just kicked in on EU, and because there were plenty of untested orders in the level I was playing off, I've already got enough of a reaction to take some profit and make the trade safe. Works every time, 80% of the time;-)

In my opinion, FTB to any level where there are large amount of untested orders is valid for a PO. Remember, all this FL/FTR analysis is merely an enhancement to basic Supply/Demand trading, and it's to help us locate the levels on the charts where the unfilled orders are. If we see an engulf in the favour of the trade first, then great - we've got a confirmed trade. However even if we don't see this, there are still many levels where we can be reasonably sure of a big bounce - certainly enough to get some profit out of, and then leave the rest to run to see what happens. These I believe are called SAS trades - "scalp and see". You'll probably never get 100% trade success with this method, but you can still take plenty of profit, and avoid taking any full stop out in most cases if you manage the trade properly.

We knew there were significant amounts of buy orders in that FL, because of how it formed - after the engulf of an important opposing level. We also could see there had been a large surge from the level. We could also see that the extreme edge of the FL had not yet been tested. All of these were good reasons to expect a reaction.

The best way to manage these types of trades for me currently is to enter the order in 2 parts. Take some profit where you see the first likely trouble area, and then hold the rest as long as PA supports it.

Seem to be at the stage now where I can pinpoint most of the minor intraday turns in the market within a few pips, by just applying a few simple rules. Many major ones too. Took a combined 40R off 2 gold shorts on Friday using the method.

- important FLs: start off on MN1, work down TFs, mark on any engulfed FTRs, or just engulfed large swings (although I don't consider the engulf of a LTF swing high/low important (unless it was a reaction to the extreme of an important FL), the return to a FTR from the engulf of a swing high/low which lasted days or weeks is going to definitely produce a tradeable reaction on LTF) - origins - SR flips from poles/last small FTR into the top/bottom

I don't trade NU, but just thought I'd open the chart and mark it up, see what's what.

This one would have been over 20R by now.

This is basically all I'm doing, every day now. I can usually hit 10R if it takes off, since the entries are so precise. Sometimes I only get a small reaction, and have to jump out at b/e. Rarely it's a complete instant loss, but I'm not too bothered about these since I can make it up so easily.

Confirmed entries are of course better using this method, but quite often you can get the first top/bottom to a few pips, and then take a second entry off what would have been your confirmed entry had you waited. This works for continuation moves also.

Find important FL; find origin; find SR flip line.
